A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CBQ and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Shared material can be matched despite substantial rewriting and experimental revisions, including smaller OPT results relocated to v2 Appendix A.2.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization experiments on OPT, BLOOM, and LLAMA, with benchmark results in Tables 1–3 and component ablations in Tables 4–7.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark, ablation, and quantization-time results in Tables 1–7, alongside retained OPT experiments in Appendix A.2.

M1.justification: The cross-block windows, homologous reconstruction, CFP, and LoRA-Rounding remain. However, the stated activation-scaling rule changes from a maximum-value ratio in v1 Eq. 5 to its square root in v2 Eq. 6. This is a localized procedural change; much of the expanded rounding and loss description documents existing components.

E1.justification: The LAMBADA evaluation reported in v1 Table 1 is removed. C4, WikiText2, PIQA, HellaSwag, ARC, Mutual, and Ethics remain, with no newly evaluated dataset or distinct task domain.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 1–2 add actual RPTQ comparisons for W4A8 OPT and QLLM comparisons for W4A4 LLAMA, and introduce GPTQ into W2A16 comparisons. The W8A8 OS+ comparisons disappear. SmoothQuant also becomes an evaluated preprocessing control in v2 Table 4, whereas its v1 participation was descriptive.

E3.justification: v2 replaces BLOOM and OPT-13B zero-shot configurations with OPT-66B and LLAMA1-65B, removes W8A8 evaluations, and expands W2A16 and W4A4 testing. Ablations switch from several BLOOM configurations to LLAMA-7B and report both C4 and WikiText2. The stated sub-4-bit activation exception changes from per-channel to per-token quantization; this wording change does not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The four existing component-ablation topics remain, but their controls expand substantially. v2 Table 4 compares CFP with SmoothQuant before and after reconstruction; Table 5 tests conventional rounding at both three and six epochs. Table 7 adds a quantization-time comparison across model sizes, extending the earlier memory and iteration analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. Both present point estimates; the new initialization details do not constitute uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Numerous benchmark and ablation entries are replaced or added, together with new timing results. For example, reported OPT-30B W2A16 C4/WikiText2 perplexities change from 11.97/9.97 to 10.92/10.26 in the respective Table 2. These are revised results, not established same-protocol gains. The smaller OPT results moved to v2 Table 9 remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Mathematical definitions change locally: v2 introduces square-root activation scaling and places the binary rounding correction inside step-size multiplication, unlike v1 Eq. 7. No theorems or proofs are added. The newly stated zero rounding initialization is inconsistent with v2 Eq. 7, whose sigmoid mapping gives 0.5 when the low-rank product is zero.

C1.justification: The principal contributions and low-bit superiority claims remain. v2 adds a concrete abstract-level efficiency claim: quantizing a 4-bit LLAMA1-65B model in 4.3 hours on one GPU. Its conclusion also emphasizes W2A16 performance and preservation of full-precision capability at W4A8/W4A16.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the expanded preprocessing experiments as showing an advantage over SmoothQuant-based reconstruction and the timing study as demonstrating greater efficiency than OmniQuant, particularly for larger models. The existing qualification that cross-block dependency cannot completely eliminate accumulated errors remains; no substantial new failure-condition analysis appears.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's calibration sample count, sequence length, window size, and epochs, v2 discloses rank 5, factor initialization, three learning rates, CosineAnnealingLR, batch size 1, single-GPU execution, and rounding-loss weight 0.01. It also reports training times. These substantially expand reproducibility information without establishing that previously undocumented settings changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds RPTQ, QLoRA, and CAQ references and explicit distinctions from AdaRound and QLoRA. The detailed introductory comparison with QLLM is removed, along with BERT, learned-step-size quantization, and LAMBADA citations. The broader positioning within reconstruction-based post-training quantization remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, and substantial portions of the method section are rewritten. The separate problem-definition subsection is absorbed into the methods introduction, an Overall loss subsection is introduced, and the appendix gains Overview and OPT-evaluation subsections. Terminology and the explanatory narrative are extensively revised.

P2.justification: v2 adds a layer/block/cross-block comparison figure, redraws the workflow and homologous-reconstruction diagrams, and reformats the retained outlier plots. Main comparison tables are extensively reorganized with highlighted CBQ rows; LLAMA results are integrated into Tables 1–2, smaller OPT results move to appendix Table 9, and a timing table is added.

improvement.justification: Actual RPTQ/QLLM comparisons, stronger preprocessing and rounding controls, and previously missing optimization settings improve empirical support and reproducibility. The net gain is limited by removed LAMBADA/BLOOM evidence, unexplained revisions to shared scores, the inconsistent rounding-initialization description, and incomplete timing comparability, including QLLM timings obtained on LLAMA2.
